body:
Part of #241. Follows #1274.

#1274 makes `shep-kelpie-dog` compile on Windows. Three pieces of its e2e run are placeholders there:

- `crates/dog/src/dog/e2e/run/deliver.rs`: the copy of the results into the worktree uses `openat` with `O_NOFOLLOW` and `unlinkat`, which have no Windows build. On Windows `deliver` returns an `unsupported` error naming this issue, so the results of an e2e run do not come back.
- `crates/dog/src/dog/e2e/stand_in.rs`: the `ssh` and `rsync` stand-ins are `sh` scripts, and `ended` probes a pid with `rustix`. On Windows `StandIn` makes the scripts without a mode, and `ended` panics.
- The e2e tests that run the stand-ins are `#[cfg_attr(windows, ignore)]`.

## What to build

- A `deliver` for Windows that refuses a reparse point (symlink or junction) at every folder on the way and at the file, and opens each file without following one. Windows has no `openat`, so this needs a handle-relative open (`NtCreateFile` with a root directory handle) or a check on the opened handle's final path
- Stand-ins for `ssh` and `rsync` that run on Windows (`write_fake` from `test_support`), and an `ended` that asks the OS whether a pid is gone
- Drop the `ignore` from the e2e tests once both exist

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `deliver` on Windows refuses a link in the worktree at the results folder, above it and inside it, as the Unix tests check
- [ ] The e2e tests run on the `windows` job without `ignore`
- [ ] `docs/design/windows.md` no longer lists the e2e delivery as unsupported


## Decisions

Triaged by the maintainer, since triage skips an issue a bot opened:

- `deliver` on Windows uses safe std only, no `NtCreateFile`. It opens each folder from the worktree down with `OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags(FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT | FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS)` and a `share_mode` without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, and refuses one whose `file_attributes()` has `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT`. It holds every handle until the copy ends, so no folder on the way can be renamed or swapped for a link meanwhile. Each file is opened the same way, and written with `create_new` after removing the old one, so a link put in its place makes the write fail
- The three flag values are local constants with a comment naming the Win32 header, so `dog` takes no new dependency
- `ended` on Windows is `!crate::tree::alive(pid)`, which `tree` already answers with `OpenProcess`. Unix keeps its `ESRCH` check
- The `ssh` and `rsync` stand-ins use `write_fake` / `write_script` from `test_support`, as `docs/design/windows.md` describes
- Not on the path to the live Windows run (#1151), so it stays `priority: P4`

## Touches

- `crates/dog/src/dog/e2e/run/deliver/windows.rs`
- `crates/dog/src/dog/e2e/stand_in.rs`
- `crates/dog/src/dog/e2e/run/tests.rs`, `crates/dog/src/dog/door/tests/e2e.rs`
- `docs/design/windows.md`
